players.product: Inference-first GPU-as-a-Service cloud on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs deployed in colocation sites; NVIDIA Cloud Partner

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance release (July 14, 2026): forward ARR of $300 million expected as of December 31, 2026, approximately 30x growth in fiscal 2026 over fiscal 2025, backed by 18 MW of data center capacity (8 MW of active HPC power and 10 MW in development under executed lease or colocation agreements), with a line of sight to 2.5 GW by year-end fiscal 2027. Active sites are in Marietta (Georgia), Kansas City (Missouri), Denver (Colorado) and two in Philadelphia, with an Oklahoma site and additional colocation partners in development; through the QAI Moon joint venture and an agreement with Connected Nation Internet Exchange Points it sees a path to 125 network-edge sites. QumulusAI houses NVIDIA Blackwell (B300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200) and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in facilities of less than 50 MW on a quarterly deployment cadence. CEO Michael Maniscalco: 'Our focus in 2026 is straightforward: bring GPU capacity online in months, not years, and convert it into durable recurring revenue.'
quarterly_data.figure: forward ARR $300 million (~30x); 18 MW by year-end 2026; line of sight to 2.5 GW by year-end fiscal 2027
